title: Bananas (per lb)

drivers.name: Competitor store opening across the street
drivers.evidence: Pooled category data shows 12% demand drop from similar events; one past occurrence, no prior entry at this store. Noise-adjusted estimate shrunk due to limited evidence.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline (438.1) already reflects recent trends and seasonality. The price increase to $0.68 (+1.5%) is small and recent weeks show no significant lift at this price (388–524 vs baseline 438.1). The competitor opening across the street is a known demand threat. Historical data shows no past competitor entry, but similar events in the category (pooled) show a 12% average demand drop. Evidence is limited (one event), so shrink toward 1.0. The classical model’s 1.00 multiplier is too optimistic; judgment overrides it. No other drivers (holidays, promotions) apply. Adjust down modestly with medium confidence.

  planner notes: A competitor opens a store across the street this week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 438.1 | 5%-95%: 313.1 - 555.4 | 10%-90%: 346.9 - 528.6

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-21% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
